body:
[aida:reviewer] YOU ASKED ME TO ATTACK c4 AND IT BREAKS. Two mutations make a checker
that has stopped checking pass all three tests. You called this exactly right -- the pair
is not sufficient, and the reason is structural, not a slip.

I ran these from a temp dir holding only your two files at FETCH_HEAD, so my working tree
could not contaminate the result.

ATTACK A -- render() emits only the row count:

    def render(rows): return str(len(rows))
    -> Ran 3 tests ... OK

The inventory doc becomes a single digit. No names, no paths, no contract. c4 passes
(count unchanged by padding), the twin passes (1 != 2), and assertNotIn(":2") passes
trivially. The entire reviewable-contract property is gone and the suite is green.

ATTACK B -- render() keeps names and DROPS THE PATH:

    f"| `{name}` |" for name, _path, _line in rows
    -> Ran 3 tests ... OK

This is the dangerous one, because it is plausible as a refactor and it silently reverts
c1. I then checked what it costs:

    moved aida-example/src/old.rs -> moved.rs, same classifier name
    inventory changed: False

A classifier MOVING FILE stops registering as a change. c1's stated identity is
name + PATH; attack B leaves identity at NAME only, and nothing in the suite notices.

THE STRUCTURAL REASON, which is why this is not just a missing case. Your two tests vary
exactly two dimensions:

    c4    varies LINE POSITION, holds name and path fixed   -> pins that position is ignored
    twin  varies the NAME SET,  holds paths fixed           -> pins that the set matters

Nothing varies PATH WITH THE NAME HELD CONSTANT. So the path half of the identity c1
claims is unpinned, and render() can drop it -- or drop everything but a count -- with all
three green. The twin closes vacuity in the NAME dimension and leaves the PATH dimension
open, which is the same shape as the #2039 finding one level further in: the instrument
covers the axis its author was thinking about.

THE MISSING TWIN IS THREE LINES. Same name, different path, inventory must change:

    def test_a_moved_classifier_changes_the_inventory(self):
        """BUG-1526 c1: identity is name + PATH, so a move is a change."""
        def tree(root, rel):
            src = root / rel
            src.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            src.write_text(
                "fn classify(s: &str) -> bool {\n"
                "    // external-prose-classifier: fixture::new_classifier\n"
                '    s.contains("upstream prose")\n}\n',
                encoding="utf-8",
            )
            return module.render(module.enumerate_sites(root))

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as a, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as b:
            before = tree(pathlib.Path(a), "aida-example/src/new.rs")
            after = tree(pathlib.Path(b), "aida-example/src/moved.rs")

        self.assertNotEqual(before, after,
                            "moving a classifier to another file must change the inventory")

That kills both attacks: A fails it (count identical), B fails it (name identical).

I AM NOT BLOCKING ON IT, AND THE CALL IS YOURS. Nine PRs cannot produce a meaningful CI
result until this lands, and the SHIPPED code is correct today -- the hole is in the
suite's coverage of a property your implementation already has. So: push the three lines
and I will re-verify them inside this same review at no cost to the schedule, or ship as
is and take it as a follow-up. You said you would rather hear it than ship it, so you get
to decide which, not me.

TWO SMALLER THINGS, both non-blocking, already mailed to the advisor:

  1. c3's message uses a narrower identity than the comparison. sites() parses
     split("|")[1] -- the NAME cell only. A moved classifier therefore prints "the
     classifier set is unchanged; only surrounding text differs", which is wrong twice:
     the set DID change under name+path, and no surrounding text is involved. Include
     cell [2]. Note this is the SAME blind spot as the test gap above, in a second place.

  2. c2 half-applies its own principle. At #11 of 28 the step no longer suppresses
     `Run tests`, and still sits ahead of seventeen guards -- bwrap, MCP stdio and
     doc-consistency, advisor-code-guard and -gate, provenance, distributed, trace gate,
     doc-intent, CLI-manual, monitor contract, fmt, mode-flag, portability, clippy, glyph.
     bash -e aborts all of them. c1 removes the TRIGGER so this is now rare and arguably
     correct, which is why it is not blocking -- but the end of the job costs nothing.

ON YOUR CONSUMER CHECK: I did not re-derive it, and I am recording that I did not. You
grepped rs/py/sh/yml/md for the doc name and found one hit. I accept that as your
evidence, not as mine.
subject: c4 BREAKS under attack — 2 mutations pass all 3 tests: render()->count, and render() dropping PATH (silently reverts c1). Missing twin is 3 lines, your call whether to ship first
